questions.q: What makes a CDC (change data capture) source connector different from a timer-based polling query, per this lesson?
options: It reads the database's own replication log directly, catching every change in order with no gap between polls and no missed deletes
It only captures inserts, never updates or deletes
It requires the database to be shut down while capturing changes
It has no meaningful difference from a polling query
questions.explain: CDC connectors like Debezium read the write-ahead log directly, which is fundamentally different from periodically querying the table.

questions.q: In this lesson's sink connector example, what does the config shape have in common with the source connector's config?
options: Both use connector.class and tasks.max — the same shape, pointed at different kinds of systems
Sink connectors never use connector.class, only source connectors do
Sink connectors require a completely different configuration language
There is no config similarity between source and sink connectors
questions.explain: Both source and sink connectors share the same fundamental config shape — connector.class and tasks.max — regardless of direction.

questions.q: When a source and sink connector are chained together, as in this lesson's Postgres-to-Snowflake example, what is NOT required?
options: A single custom producer or consumer written for either hop
Any Kafka topic in between the two connectors
Any configuration for either connector
Any monitoring of the pipeline's running status
questions.explain: Both hops are Connect configuration, not custom client code — that's the whole value of chaining connectors this way.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how does a sink connector into a data warehouse compare to using Structured Streaming (Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 33) for the same goal?
options: A sink connector solves the same "get data into my analytics system" problem via configuration, without a Spark job to write and maintain
Structured Streaming and sink connectors solve completely unrelated problems
A sink connector can only write to Kafka topics, never to a warehouse
Structured Streaming replaces the need for Kafka Connect entirely in all cases
questions.explain: Both are valid ways to land streaming data into an analytics system — a sink connector avoids writing and maintaining a Spark job for that specific case.

questions.q: What does the Confluent Cloud screenshot in this lesson actually show?
options: A real running connector's status on the Connectors page
A diagram illustrating the concept of source versus sink connectors
The Schema Registry's tree view of registered schemas
A code editor showing Debezium's source code
questions.explain: It's a genuine screenshot of a real, running connector's status, not an illustration of the source/sink concept.
